question: Propose the most cost-effective measurable leading indicator for the stated failure, its operating threshold, and the concrete test that would validate or kill the predictor.
device: shell-and-tube condenser on a steam turbine exhaust, 300 MW unit
failure: tube-side biofouling accumulates over weeks; heat transfer degrades causing turbine back-pressure rise and derating
followup_finding: The condenser U-coefficient fell 18% from baseline 22 days before the last back-pressure derate. Tube-bundle fouling resistance was confirmed at 0.0012 m2K/W by the subsequent cleaning inspection.
constraint: predictor must use existing temperature and flow measurements only, fire at least 3 weeks before back-pressure hits the derating limit, no requirement for new instrumentation
user_variables: no false trips during load swings
round1_answer:
Nonlinear gain modulation via hyperbolic tangent function to enhance damping and transient shaping in control loops

Implement a tanh-based nonlinear feedback loop on the existing cooling water flow measurement to dynamically adjust the condenser pressure control setpoint, compensating for the gradual fouling resistance rise

Maintain stable back-pressure by actively modulating the pressure control response as the U-coefficient degrades, extending time-to-derating event

Run a closed-loop simulation where a step fault in fouling resistance is introduced; verify that the tanh-PID controller maintains pressure deviation within 0.5% of baseline, whereas the legacy linear PID exhibits overshoot exceeding 2%

Maintains U-coefficient integrity by triggering back-pressure mitigation protocols 3 weeks before the derating limit is reached, specifically identifying the 18% U-coefficient drop as the early warning trigger.
